title: NCL Mine Surveyor Mock 13
pattern: 100 MCQs, 100 marks, 90 min, NO negative marking

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'nautical almanac' provides:
options: Positions of celestial bodies for given dates and times
questions.solution: The Nautical Almanac tabulates the Greenwich hour angle and declination of the Sun, Moon, planets, and navigational stars.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: 'Competent person' under the Mines Act 1952 means a person:
options: Appointed by the owner, agent or manager and possessing the prescribed qualifications
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.2(1)(c): a competent person is one appointed by the owner, agent or manager with the prescribed qualifications for the purpose.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Local Apparent Time (LAT) is determined directly from the hour angle of the:
questions.solution: LAT = 12h + hour angle of the Sun (expressed in time); it is the time indicated by a sundial.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The Greenwich Hour Angle (GHA) of a star is obtained from:
options: The Nautical Almanac for a given UT
questions.solution: GHA is tabulated in the almanac for selected stars and the Sun at specific Universal Times.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A first-aid room is required at a mine where the number of persons employed exceeds:
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.21: a first-aid room is required where more than 150 persons are employed.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Approaching a goaf, probing shall be carried out ahead of the working for at least:
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 147: the working is probed ahead for at least 1.5 m beyond the last support before approaching the goaf.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Mean Right Ascension of Aries (ν) is used to convert between:
questions.solution: ν (or GHA Aries) bridges the equatorial and horizontal coordinate systems; LHA = GHA + local longitude.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'meridian passage' of a star occurs when its hour angle is:
questions.solution: Upper culmination: LHA = 0h; lower culmination: LHA = 12h.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: For observations near the horizon, atmospheric refraction can amount to approximately:
questions.solution: At the geometric horizon, standard refraction is about 34 arc-minutes (nearly the Sun's diameter).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: While driving approaching old or waterlogged workings, advance boreholes shall be kept at least ______ ahead of the face.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 163: at least 3 advance boreholes not less than 3 m ahead of the face, with flank holes within 5 m on either side.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Time can be determined by the 'method of equal altitudes' using the:
options: Any star observed at equal altitudes east and west of meridian
Any star observed rising and setting
questions.solution: When a star reaches the same altitude on both sides of the meridian, the mean of the two times gives local mean time.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The precession in right ascension per year is approximately:
questions.solution: General precession in RA is about 3.07s per year (approx 46 arcsec per year).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'chronometer' used in surveying typically keeps:
questions.solution: A marine/survey chronometer is set to GMT (UTC) so that local observations can be compared with almanac data.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: To convert local sidereal time to local mean solar time, one uses:
questions.solution: Sidereal-to-solar conversion tables (or the formula LST = 1.0027379 × LMT + ν) are used.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'semi-diameter' correction is needed when observing the Sun because:
options: We observe the limb, not the centre
questions.solution: The observed altitude is to the upper or lower limb; the semi-diameter (~16') must be applied to get the centre.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Proper motion of a star is the apparent angular motion due to:
options: The star's actual space velocity relative to the Sun
questions.solution: Proper motion is the star's actual movement across the sky over years, distinct from apparent diurnal motion.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'refraction constant' at sea level at standard temperature is about:
questions.solution: At the horizon, standard refraction is ~34'; at 45° altitude it is about 1'; the constant varies with altitude.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: As per the Mines Act 1952, women may be employed aboveground only between:
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.46: women shall not be employed belowground, and aboveground employment is restricted between 6 a.m. and 7 p.m.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'position angle' of a binary star system refers to:
options: The angle from north to the companion star measured at the primary
questions.solution: Position angle is measured from north through east to the secondary star as seen from the primary.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Ephemeris time was introduced to replace UT because:
options: UT varied unpredictably due to tidal deceleration
questions.solution: ET (now TT) was based on planetary motions and free from the irregularities of Earth's rotation that affect UT.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'transit instrument' is used to determine:
options: Time and right ascension by observing meridian crossings
questions.solution: A transit telescope observes stars crossing the meridian, providing precise time and RA.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'aberration constant' is approximately:
questions.solution: The constant of aberration kappa is approximately 20.5 arcseconds due to Earth mean orbital velocity.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The maximum working hours in a week for an adult employed belowground in a mine are:
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.28: no person shall be employed belowground for more than 48 hours in any week.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Under the Mines Act 1952, notice of which of the following accidents is required to be given to the prescribed authorities?
options: Loss of life, serious bodily injury, explosion, ignition, fire, inrush of water or other matter
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.23: notice is required for loss of life, serious injury, and specified occurrences such as explosion, ignition, fire, inrush of water.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'latitude by Polaris' method gives latitude directly from the altitude because Polaris is:
options: Within ~0.7° of the pole, with tabulated corrections
Exactly at the north celestial pole
questions.solution: Polaris is close to but not exactly at the pole; tables give corrections based on LHA of Aries.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'azimuth by Polaris' method requires knowing the observer's:
options: Latitude and the star's hour angle
questions.solution: Azimuth of Polaris is computed from its hour angle and the observer's latitude.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The diurnal rotation of the Earth causes stars to appear to move:
questions.solution: Earth rotates eastward, so stars appear to move east to west across the sky.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'zenith distance' of a star is:
questions.solution: Zenith distance z = 90° - altitude (h); it is the angular distance from the zenith.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: For precise time determination, the 'chronograph' records the exact time of:
questions.solution: A chronograph registers the instant a star crosses the transit wire, compared with chronometer time.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'colatitude' of a place is:
questions.solution: Colatitude = 90° - φ; it is the zenith distance of the celestial pole.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: As per CMR 2017, every plan and section at a mine shall be:
options: Serially numbered and stored flat, with indexed field books kept at the mine
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 68: plans and sections are serially numbered, stored flat, and field books indexed and kept at the mine office.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A map projection is a systematic transformation of:
options: Three-dimensional ellipsoidal coordinates to a two-dimensional plane
questions.solution: Projections convert 3D (lat, lon, height) to 2D (E, N) on a map plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Under the Mines Act 1952, an Inspector may, among other powers:
options: Enter, inspect and examine a mine, and make inquiries on any matter relating to safety
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.22: Inspectors may enter, inspect, examine and inquire into any mine and its records.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A conformal projection preserves:
options: Angles and shapes of small features
questions.solution: Conformal projections preserve local angles; small shapes are maintained.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An equal-area projection preserves:
questions.solution: Equal-area (equivalent) projections maintain proportional areas across the map.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) system divides the Earth into how many zones?
questions.solution: UTM has 60 longitudinal zones, each 6° wide.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Each UTM zone spans how many degrees of longitude?
questions.solution: UTM zones are 6° wide, numbered 1 to 60 east from 180°W.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The central meridian of a UTM zone has a false easting of:
questions.solution: The central meridian is assigned a false easting of 500,000 m to avoid negative coordinates.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The scale factor at the central meridian of UTM is:
questions.solution: UTM uses a scale factor of 0.9996 at the central meridian, giving two lines of true scale at ~180 km either side.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The false northing for UTM in the southern hemisphere is:
questions.solution: In the southern hemisphere, a false northing of 10,000,000 m is applied so that all northing values are positive.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The Lambert Conformal Conic projection is best suited for regions that are:
options: Long east-west and moderate latitude extent
Very large and spanning many latitudes
questions.solution: Lambert conformal conic is ideal for mid-latitude regions with greater east-west than north-south extent.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'standard parallels' of a conic projection are where:
questions.solution: Standard parallels are the lines where the projection surface intersects the ellipsoid, giving scale factor = 1.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Scale distortion on a map projection increases with distance from:
options: The standard parallels or central meridian
questions.solution: Distortion grows as you move away from the lines (or point) of true scale.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Cassini' projection is:
questions.solution: Cassini is a transverse cylindrical projection that is equidistant along the central meridian and perpendicular lines.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'Tissot's indicatrix' on a map projection shows:
options: Distortion in scale and shape at each point
questions.solution: Tissot ellipses show local distortion; circles on the sphere appear as ellipses on the projection.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'gnomonic' projection has the property that:
options: All great circles appear as straight lines
questions.solution: On a gnomonic projection, every great circle projects as a straight line, useful for navigation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'stereographic' projection is:
options: Perspective from the centre of the Earth
questions.solution: Stereographic is a conformal azimuthal projection; circles on the sphere map to circles on the plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: For a Transverse Mercator projection, the line of true scale is:
options: Two lines parallel to the central meridian
questions.solution: In TM the central meridian has scale factor < 1; two lines at ~180 km have true scale.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Lambert Equal Area' projection is commonly used for:
options: Statistical and thematic maps requiring area comparison
questions.solution: Equal-area projections are preferred for statistical maps where area comparisons must be accurate.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Mollweide' projection is:
questions.solution: Mollweide is a pseudocylindrical equal-area projection used for world maps.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Mercator' projection is:
questions.solution: Mercator is conformal; rhumb lines are straight but it severely distorts area near poles.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On a Mercator projection, the spacing of parallels:
questions.solution: Parallels are spaced increasingly apart toward the poles to maintain conformality.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'geodetic datum' defines:
options: The reference ellipsoid and its position/orientation relative to the Earth
questions.solution: A datum specifies the ellipsoid (shape) and its spatial relationship (position and orientation) to the Earth.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The WGS 84 datum uses the ellipsoid parameters:
questions.solution: WGS 84 uses a = 6,378,137 m and 1/f = 298.257223563, essentially identical to GRS 80.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'datum shift' is required when converting coordinates between:
questions.solution: Coordinates on one datum (e.g., Everest 1830) must be transformed to another (e.g., WGS 84) using shift parameters.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Molodensky' transformation is used for:
questions.solution: Molodensky formulas convert between datums using differences in ellipsoid parameters and datum shift (dX, dY, dZ).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The seven-parameter 'Helmert' transformation involves:
options: Three translations, three rotations, and one scale factor
questions.solution: The Helmert (Bursa-Wolf) transformation uses 3 translations, 3 rotations, and 1 scale change.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'geoid-ellipsoid separation' (geoid undulation) is the distance between:
options: The ground surface and sea level
The geoid (mean sea level surface) and the reference ellipsoid
questions.solution: Geoid undulation N = h (ellipsoidal height) - H (orthometric height).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: GPS provides heights relative to:
questions.solution: GPS gives ellipsoidal height h; geoid undulation must be subtracted to get orthometric height H.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'combined scale factor' (CSF) in surveying accounts for:
options: Both the projection scale factor and the elevation factor
questions.solution: CSF = map scale factor × elevation (gravity) factor; it converts ground distances to grid distances.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When workings approach within 60 m of a water body or waterlogged area, the manager shall:
options: Stop working immediately without any plan
Leave the water body untouched forever
Only mark it on the board
Prepare a scheme for protection against inrush and drain the water in a planned manner
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 149 (danger from surface water) & Ch. XI: within 60 m, protective schemes (drainage, barriers) are implemented.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'grid factor' (or 'map scale factor') converts:
questions.solution: Grid factor accounts for the projection distortion at a point, converting ground (ellipsoid) to grid distance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: On the UTM projection, the maximum scale distortion within a zone is approximately:
questions.solution: UTM limits distortion to ~0.04% (factor 0.9996 at CM, ~1.0004 at zone edges).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Cassini-Soldner' projection was historically used for:
options: Large-scale topographic maps in some countries
questions.solution: Cassini was used for topographic mapping in the UK, India, and other countries before TM became standard.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Oblique Mercator' projection is used for:
options: Regions that are elongated along a great circle not aligned with meridians or equator
questions.solution: Oblique Mercator is used for features (e.g., Malaysia, Borneo) that trend oblique to meridians.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In the Indian context, the 'Indian 1975' datum is based on the:
questions.solution: Indian datum 1975 uses the Everest 1830 ellipsoid with a defined origin at Kandla.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Survey of India' topographic maps use which projection?
questions.solution: Historically, Survey of India 1:50,000 and 1:250,000 maps use the Polyconic projection.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In return airways and old workings, the air shall normally contain oxygen not less than ______ and carbon dioxide not more than ______.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 165: not less than 19% oxygen and not more than 0.5% carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Transverse Mercator' zone width can be reduced to 3° (Modified TM) to:
questions.solution: Narrower zones (e.g., 3°) reduce maximum scale distortion, improving accuracy.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Cassini' projection is equidistant along:
options: The central meridian and lines perpendicular to it
questions.solution: Cassini preserves distances along the central meridian and along lines perpendicular (transverse) to it.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'grid bearing' differs from a 'geodetic bearing' by:
questions.solution: Grid bearing = geodetic bearing ± convergence angle γ (due to meridians converging toward the pole).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'meridian convergence' (γ) is zero at:
questions.solution: At the equator, meridians are parallel, so convergence is zero; it increases toward the poles.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'false origin' (false easting and northing) is applied to:
questions.solution: False origins ensure all grid coordinates within a zone are positive, avoiding negative numbers.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'International 1924' (Hayford) ellipsoid has a flattening of:
questions.solution: The International ellipsoid: a = 6,378,388 m, 1/f = 297 (approximately).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the percentage of inflammable gas in the general body of air exceeds ______, persons shall be withdrawn from the working.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 166: persons are withdrawn when the general body of air exceeds 1.25% inflammable gas.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Lambert projection' with two standard parallels is also called:
questions.solution: When the projection cone cuts through the ellipsoid (two standard parallels), it is a secant projection.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'UTM grid convergence' at a point is the angle between:
questions.solution: Grid convergence γ = angle between grid north (y-axis) and true (geodetic) north (meridian).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'arc-to-chord' (reduction to chord) correction is needed because:
options: A geodetic line on the ellipsoid is a great circle, not a straight line on the projection
questions.solution: The projection of a geodetic line onto the map is curved; the straight chord on the map differs from the projected arc.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'geodetic coordinate system' uses which axes?
options: X toward Greenwich, Y toward 90°E, Z toward North Pole
X toward North Pole, Y toward Greenwich, Z toward 90°E
X east, Y north, Z up
questions.solution: Geocentric: X through (φ=0, λ=0), Y through (φ=0, λ=90°E), Z through North Pole.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'azimuth' on the UTM grid is measured from:
questions.solution: Grid azimuth is measured clockwise from the grid north direction (parallel to the y-axis of the projection).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The average of three numbers is 40. The first number is twice the second and the second is thrice the third. What is the first number?
questions.solution: Let third = x, second = 3x, first = 6x. (6x + 3x + x)/3 = 40 → 10x = 120 → x = 12. First = 72

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: A man walks at 5 km/h for 6 hours and then at 4 km/h for 4 hours. What is his average speed?
questions.solution: Total distance = 30 + 16 = 46 km. Total time = 10 hours. Average = 4.6 km/h

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: A 300 m train crosses a 200 m platform in 25 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.solution: Distance = 500 m. Speed = 500/25 = 20 m/s = 72 km/h

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Two trains start from the same point at 60 km/h and 40 km/h in the same direction. How long will they take to be 100 km apart?
questions.solution: Relative speed = 60 - 40 = 20 km/h. Time = 100/20 = 5 hours

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The average of three numbers is 40. The first two numbers are 30 and 45. What is the third number?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: If A:B = 3:4 and B:C = 2:5, what is A:B:C?
questions.solution: B is common. LCM of 4 and 2 = 4. A:B = 3:4, B:C = 4:10. A:B:C = 3:4:10.

questions.stem: What is the LCM of 12, 18, and 24?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: What is the unit digit of 7^2023?
questions.solution: Unit digits cycle: 7,9,3,1. 2023 mod 4 = 3. So unit digit = 3. Wait: 7^1=7, 7^2=9, 7^3=3, 7^4=1. 2023÷4 = 505 remainder 3. So unit digit = 3. Answer should be B.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: What is the area of a rectangle with length 12 cm and breadth 8 cm?
questions.solution: Area = 12×8 = 96 cm².

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: What is the circumference of a circle with radius 7 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution: Circumference = 2πr = 2×22/7×7 = 44 cm.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The diagonal of a square is 10√2 cm. What is its area?
questions.solution: Diagonal = a√2 = 10√2 → a=10. Area = a² = 100 cm².

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the hypotenuse?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The volume of a cube is 64 cm³. What is its surface area?
questions.solution: Side = ∛64 = 4 cm. Surface area = 6×4² = 96 cm².
